explanation: He and his followers were called Cynics, from the Greek for 'dog-like'. Legend says that when Alexander the Great offered him any favour, he asked him to stand out of his sunlight.

claims.text: According to ancient accounts, Diogenes of Sinope lived in a large clay jar (a pithos) in Athens.
Socrates, Epicurus and Pythagoras are not said to have lived in a jar.
The name Cynic comes from the Greek kynikos, 'dog-like'.
A famous anecdote says that when Alexander the Great offered Diogenes a favour, he asked Alexander to stand out of his sunlight.
